nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Sunshine powers the grasses and wildflowers that feed everything else on the prairie.

nodes.name: Rain & snow
nodes.desc: The park gets roughly 21 inches of precipitation a year, plus heavy winter snow, which is modest water for grassland growth.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Grassland fire clears dead growth and holds back woody plants, one of the forces that keeps prairie open.

nodes.name: Prairie soil
nodes.desc: Nutrients released by decay return to the soil and feed the next season of plant growth.

nodes.name: Blue grama & buffalo grass
nodes.desc: Short grasses that prairie dogs favour and that bison graze in mixed-grass prairie.

nodes.name: Western wheatgrass
nodes.desc: A cool-season grass of the northern Great Plains, a staple for grazers and a main food of prairie dogs.

nodes.name: Prairie wildflowers
nodes.desc: Coneflowers, globemallow and other forbs add diversity to the grassland and feed pronghorn and prairie dogs.

nodes.name: Chokecherry
nodes.desc: A thicket-forming shrub of draws and slopes whose leaves and fruit are eaten by deer and other animals.

nodes.name: Ponderosa pine
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the hills, forming the forest that meets the prairie at the park edge.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: The park herd is one of four free-roaming, genetically pure bison herds on public land. They graze mainly grasses and sedges.

nodes.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
nodes.desc: A burrowing grazer that lives in large colonies; its digging and clipping reshape vegetation and its colonies support many other species.

nodes.name: Pronghorn
nodes.desc: A fast grassland ungulate that lives in the park alongside bison and elk.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Elk graze and browse in the park, and are among the larger prey of mountain lions.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: A browsing deer of slopes and pine edges, taken by cougars and coyotes.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed- and insect-eating rodent that is prey for badgers, coyotes, snakes and ferrets.

nodes.name: Black-footed ferret
nodes.desc: An endangered weasel that depends on prairie dog colonies, which can make up most of its diet. The species has been reintroduced to the park.

nodes.name: American badger
nodes.desc: A digging carnivore that preys on prairie dogs and other burrowing rodents.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A generalist predator of prairie dogs, rodents and young ungulates that also scavenges.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor that hunts rodents, birds and eggs in grassland.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that finds and eats carcasses of deer and small mammals.

nodes.name: Black-billed Magpie
nodes.desc: A clever corvid that feeds on carrion as well as insects and seeds.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The park apex predator, which takes mainly deer and elk and is regarded as a keystone species.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down carcasses, dung and dead grass, returning nutrients to the soil.
